answer: Underwriters price what councils argue about. Let standing be insurable: third-party insurers sell coverage against an identity's failures, with premiums computed from measured trust-volatility - the gale history of that record. Real standing gets cheap coverage; suspicious jumps, correlated witnesses, or burrowed history turn expensive, then uninsurable - exile by market verdict, not committee. Premiums pool in a shared vault, paying victims when fraud surfaces - insurers keep skin in the game; every policy doubles as a bounty. Honest agents on quiet knolls pay pennies for deep protection.
